ablation_plan: Compare the inherited constructor alone against the constructor plus direct single-vertex reassignment.
Compare direct reassignment against direct reassignment plus Kempe-chain interchange while keeping pass order and stopping bounds fixed.
Disable smallest-terminal-class prioritization while retaining the same recoloring neighborhood to test whether objective-directed targeting causes any color-count change.
assumptions: SEED produces a deterministic valid coloring that can be post-processed in baseline.py.
The frozen evaluator permits bounded deterministic post-processing within its execution budget.
failure_risks: Kempe-chain swaps may not unlock elimination of any color class on the frozen development graphs.
The added deterministic search may increase runtime without changing color counts.
A faulty component swap or recoloring could produce an invalid coloring.
candidate.falsifier: Falsified if deterministic development-only evaluation shows neither lower mean_color_count nor higher relative_improvement versus SEED, or if invalid_coloring_rate or nonreproducible_rate exceeds 0.0.
candidate.hypothesis: Adding deterministic, objective-directed Kempe-chain post-processing to the inherited constructor will eliminate a terminal color class on some frozen public development instances, reducing valid color counts relative to SEED.
candidate.intervention: In tasks/graph_coloring/candidates/baseline.py, retain the inherited constructor and add a bounded deterministic post-processing phase. Repeatedly target the smallest color class among classes using the highest color index. For each target vertex, first try direct reassignment to a lower color; when blocked, enumerate lower-color pairs and interchange the induced two-color Kempe component if doing so makes a lower color available. Accept only validity-preserving moves, compact labels after eliminating a class, and use fixed iteration and tie-breaking order.
mechanism_claims: Swapping the two colors within an induced Kempe component preserves coloring validity.
A Kempe interchange can alter the lower colors blocking a target vertex and enable a reassignment unavailable to single-vertex greedy repair.
Targeting the smallest highest-index class directs the neighborhood search toward eliminating one complete color class.
